KAZ.hook: The largest landlocked country in the world — bigger than all of Western Europe, and Russia's border with it is the longest continuous land border anywhere.
KAZ.place: The vast steppe below Russia, stretching from the Caspian east to China.
KAZ.borders: The Kazakh SSR's line, consolidated by 1936 to bundle the steppe peoples — including a terrain-free line across open grassland that became, in 1991, the world's longest continuous land border, with Russia.

UZB.hook: One of only two doubly landlocked countries on Earth — every route to the sea crosses at least two borders. The other is Liechtenstein.
UZB.place: The centre of Central Asia, touching all four of its neighbours and Afghanistan.
UZB.borders: The centrepiece of Stalin's 1924 'national delimitation': republic lines drawn valley by valley and village by village, producing the Fergana Valley's interlocking jigsaw with Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan — enclaves included — and a country that touches all four other -stans.

TKM.hook: The Darvaza gas crater has been burning since 1971, when geologists set it alight expecting it to go out in weeks.
TKM.place: On the Caspian's eastern shore, mostly the Karakum desert, below Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan.
TKM.borders: The 1924 delimitation assigned the Turkmen lands between the Caspian, the Amu Darya and the Kopet Dag mountains; the Iranian line along those mountains descends from Russo-Persian treaties of the 1880s.

TJK.hook: Over 90% mountain — the Pamirs are so high and remote the road through them is nicknamed the roof of the world.
TJK.place: The southeastern corner of Central Asia, squeezed between Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan, China and Afghanistan.
TJK.borders: The mountain remainder of the 1924–29 carve-up: it received the high Pamirs but not Samarkand and Bukhara, the historic Tajik-speaking cities left in Uzbekistan — and its Fergana valley edges stayed contested into the 2020s.

KGZ.hook: Lake Issyk-Kul is the second-largest mountain lake in the world and never freezes, despite sitting at 1,600m in the Tian Shan.
KGZ.place: The mountainous strip along China's western border, above Tajikistan.
KGZ.borders: Drawn around the Tian Shan in the Soviet delimitation; its rim of the Fergana Valley interlocks so tightly with Uzbek and Tajik territory that the last disputed stretches with Tajikistan were only settled by treaty in 2025.
